question: The path that keeps the most time

scene.title: The path that keeps the most time
scene.subtitle: Height gains time, speed loses it. The arc a ball really follows is the best trade.
scene.takeaway: A falling ball is not pushed. It follows the path between two moments that keeps the most time.

beats.title: No gravity: stay put
beats.body: Without gravity, a thrown clock only loses time by moving, so staying put keeps the most time.

beats.title: Turn gravity on
beats.body: Now clocks run faster higher up, so going up gains time. But getting there means moving fast, which loses time. A low throw gains little, and a high throw loses too much.

beats.title: The best trade
beats.body: The path that keeps the most time is exactly the arc a thrown ball follows. Change the gravity and the best arc changes with it.

scene.why: It links falling to time: the arc a thrown ball follows is exactly the path along which its clock gains the most time.
scene.opening: Of all the paths a ball could take between the throw and the catch, why does it follow that particular arc?

questions.q: A clock is tossed up and caught. Does it show more or less time than an identical clock held still?
questions.a: More. It spends time higher up, where clocks run faster, which outweighs what it loses by moving.

questions.q: If higher clocks run faster, why doesn’t the ball fly much higher?
questions.a: Going higher means moving faster on the way, and speed loses time. The real arc is the best balance.

questions.q: With no gravity at all, which path keeps the most time?
questions.a: Staying put: without height to gain, any movement only loses time.
